items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: The interviewer mentions 'Faby' in a question about American composers, but Louis Armstrong does not mention Faby in his response, nor does he indicate any personal interaction or specific knowledge of the individual beyond the context of the question.

ctx.x: Yes, of course. We serious. Sure, we serious. It wasn't but a scene. About two choruses. But the way they were swinging. Watch. Da-da-da. Da-da-da. No. They was wailing. We wailed with them. That's what gave Custer that bad day. You playing the trumpet. We didn't. We didn't. But the audience made us play it six times. Heritage with Louis Armstrong will continue in just one moment. Please stand by. Louis Armstrong will resume in just one moment. Please bear with us. The Indian turned around and said, Where did all…
I mean, Faby has only very little time left. Mr. Armstrong, this is interesting. Of the American composers today, saying the symphonic theme or an opera, who do you like best?

Even when I was in school, I played all classical music. When I was in the orphanage, we played duets. And that was the music. So that instills the soul in you. You know? Litz, Bach, Bach, Marnonoff, Gustav Mahler, and Haydn. We had a little laugh there, where he kept on saying, Haydn, Haydn. And I said, well, let him come out. You know? That was Haydn's style, too. He'd surprise you any time. Every composer that there was, we used it in this song. I'm glad you mentioned Mahler. He's one of my favorite composers.…
